The United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women’s Club World Cup from January 5 to 30, 2028, with Arsenal among seven clubs already confirmed for the historic tournament. As reported by BBC Sport on Thursday, FIFA confirmed that the 19-team competition will take place every four years, following a format similar to the revamped men’s Club World Cup. Arsenal, Barcelona, Gotham FC, Club América, Corinthians, Naegohyang and Wuhan Jiangda have secured places in the tournament, while the remaining 12 teams will be determined at a later date. The United States was selected to host the competition following its recent experience staging major international football tournaments, alongside growing interest in women’s football and its established sporting infrastructure. FIFA chief women’s football officer Sarai Bareman said the country was the standout choice to host the inaugural edition. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Ultimately, the United States’ recent excellence in staging top Fifa tournaments, combined with the significant interest in women’s football there plus its elite sporting infrastructure, made the country the standout option,” Bareman said. She added that the tournament would provide clubs with an opportunity to showcase their quality and reach new audiences around the world. “These seven clubs, and a dozen more, will come together to show the strength and depth of women’s club football to a global audience,” she said. They have thoroughly earned this opportunity to be part of history in the United States.” Six additional European clubs will qualify to represent UEFA, while the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Confederation of African Football (CAF), Concacaf and South American Football Confederation (CONMEBOL) will each have three representatives. Oceania’s football confederation (OFC) will have one club. The United States hosted the men’s Club World Cup in 2025 and is also set to co-host the men’s FIFA World Cup in 2026 alongside Mexico and Canada. The country will further host the 2031 Women’s World Cup alongside Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico. However, the scheduling of the new women’s competition has raised concerns within the domestic game. Earlier this year, the Women’s Super League (WSL) described the timing of the Club World Cup as potentially “catastrophic”, amid concerns about the impact of another major competition during the women’s football calendar. The tournament will be the second new mid-season women’s club competition introduced by FIFA in recent years, following the launch of the Women’s Champions Cup, which was held for the first time in February and won by Arsenal.
